details:
- CVE-2026-85501: Crafted DNSSEC zones could make the validator do excessive
  work (Retrap); new val-validation-attempts and val-hash-attempts limits.
- CVE-2023-50387: Validating many DNSKEYs and RRSIGs could exhaust CPU
  (KeyTrap).
- CVE-2023-50868: NSEC3 closest encloser proofs could exhaust CPU.
- CVE-2026-33278: The copy of a suspended DS reply overwrote its rrset array
  pointer: memory corruption.
- CVE-2022-3204: Non-responsive delegations could make the resolver do unbounded
  target lookups (NRDelegation).
- CVE-2019-16866: A malformed NOTIFY query left the EDNS data uninitialised;
  such queries now get FORMERR.
- CVE-2026-41292: Long lists of EDNS options were parsed with quadratic cost;
  parsing stops after 100 options.
- CVE-2026-42959: The validator filled the additional section of the chase reply
  at the wrong offset.
- CVE-2026-81634: DNSSEC canonicalization wrote signature and name data into the
  buffer without size checks: heap buffer overflow.
- CVE-2026-40622: A more trusted NS RRset could extend the lifetime of a cached
  delegation (ghost domain).
- CVE-2025-5994: With subnetcache, replies without ECS were stored in the global
  cache (Rebirthday cache poisoning).
- CVE-2026-44690: With aggressive-nsec, wildcard answers were cached before the
  proof was checked and across zones: cache poisoning.
